pins.name: National Museum of Korea (국립중앙박물관)
pins.desc: Seobinggo-ro 137, Yongsan. Korea's biggest museum, and a good rainy-day base: you can spend a whole day inside. Reports say it had about 6.5 million visitors in 2025, third in the world. Ichon Station is right next to it. Hours (per Naver, 2026-10-24): Wed and Sat 09:30–21:00, other days 09:30–17:30. Entry to the permanent exhibitions is free; special exhibitions can have a ticket.

pins.name: War Memorial of Korea (전쟁기념관)
pins.desc: Itaewon-ro 29, Yongsan. The museum of Korea's wars, with a large outdoor display of real aircraft and tanks, so it is best in dry weather, with the indoor halls as the rainy-day part. Hours (per Naver, 2026-10-24): 09:30–17:40, closed every Monday. Entry is free.

pins.name: Leeum Museum of Art (리움미술관)
pins.desc: Itaewon-ro 55-gil 60-16, Hannam-dong. Traditional Korean art and modern and contemporary art side by side, in buildings by three famous architects. Hours (per Naver, 2026-10-24): 10:00–18:00, closed every Monday. Ticket prices change by exhibition, so check Naver before you go.

pins.name: MMCA Seoul, National Museum of Modern and Contemporary Art (국립현대미술관 서울)
pins.desc: Samcheong-ro 30, Samcheong-dong. Korea's national modern and contemporary art museum, a short walk from the Samcheong-dong part of our Hanok Villages walk. Reports say it had about 2.1 million visitors in 2025. Hours (per Naver, 2026-10-24): 10:00–18:00, open until 21:00 on Wed and Sat. Ticket prices change by exhibition, so check Naver.

pins.name: National Folk Museum of Korea (국립민속박물관)
pins.desc: Samcheong-ro 37, next to Gyeongbokgung. Everyday life in Korea through history: clothes, food, festivals and houses. An easy first museum for visitors. Hours (per Naver, 2026-10-24): 09:00–18:00, open until 20:00 on Wed. Entry is free.

pins.name: Seoul Museum of History (서울역사박물관)
pins.desc: Saemunan-ro 55, Jongno-gu, near Gwanghwamun and Gyeonghuigung Palace. The story of Seoul from its early days to today, with a big model of the city. A good one if you want to understand the city you are walking through. Hours (per Naver, 2026-10-24): 09:00–21:00, Thursday 09:00–18:00, closed every Monday. Entry to the permanent exhibition is free.

pins.name: National Palace Museum of Korea (국립고궁박물관)
pins.desc: Hyoja-ro 12, Jongno-gu, right beside Gyeongbokgung. Treasures of the Joseon royal court: royal seals, clothing, furniture and ceremonial objects. A good pair with a palace visit. Hours (per Naver, 2026-10-24): Wed and Sat 09:30–21:00, other days 09:30–17:30. Naver shows it closed on Monday 26 Oct, so check the regular closed days before you go. Entry is free. Tip: Free locker room.

pins.name: National Museum of Korean Contemporary History (대한민국역사박물관)
pins.desc: Sejong-daero 198, by Gwanghwamun Square. Korea's modern and contemporary history, from the late 1800s to today, told with objects and photos. Hours (per Naver, 2026-10-24): 10:00–18:00, open until 21:00 on Wed and Sat. Reports say entry to the permanent exhibition is free; check Naver for special shows.

pins.name: Forest Herbal Land, charcoal-kiln spa (숲속한방랜드)
pins.desc: Bongwonsa-gil 75-7, Seodaemun-gu, near Sinchon. A jjimjilbang (Korean bathhouse) in the woods, and one of the best ways to warm up on a cold day. Reports say it has charcoal kilns outdoors, which is unusual for a city spa. Hours (per Naver, 2026-10-24): daily 06:30–22:00. Check Naver for prices and what to bring.
